coverage_note: Many stretches are Latin-transliterated Medi Arabic (04:06-04:28, 06:14-08:04, 09:54-11:57, 25:15-26:47) and several lines are engine-garbled (tinnis be mayi, بأسب = batdaya2, daia et = daya2et, أسر مارا الجاي, النوراح, مواسف/ياسر, حندارة). No echo-candidates file existed for this date. Name check: كانوا in this lesson is the verb 'were', not Kano. Left out on purpose: 'last kind' vs 'last one' (17:52-18:21, Amal says both fine); 40:00 قرأت (Amal repeated it, he said it right); تانية vs تانين (46:48-47:39, Amal says تانية is valid); 'costume' (not on her sheet, so not tier 3); 49:15-49:51 إشي المفضل عندي (Amal said صح). 30:20 and 44:17 may be his own self-fixes (low confidence). Several fixes are Amal's English prompts (13:44, 24:15, 30:22, 42:31).

rows.medi_said: الواجب عندو تلات سو-- أسول-- أو-- Hold on. أسئلة.
rows.amal_said: صح. فيو ثلاث أسئلة. / فيو، in it. / It doesn't have. There's in it.
rows.why: He used 'has' (عندو) for 'the homework has three questions'; Amal supplied فيو (in it) and said 'It doesn't have'.

rows.medi_said: أمها أو أبوها. ... Aunts and uncles.
rows.amal_said: أوه، عمها وعمتها. Cuz ولاد أمها are أخوتها.
rows.why: He wanted aunts and uncles but said her mother or father; Amal supplied عمها وعمتها (sheet: عمة aunt paternal).

rows.medi_said: أنا بحكي--
rows.why: Talking about yesterday he began in the present (بحكي); Amal cut in 'وأنا؟' and he restarted with past حكيت. May be his own restart.
rows.english: I spoke a lot of Arabic.

rows.medi_said: Uh, their ahel hom, uh, yehku inglisi ma hom.
rows.why: Plain present 'their parents speak English' without b- (b-drop is only after modals); Amal let it pass.
rows.english: Their parents speak English with them.

rows.medi_said: bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom ... Uh, rah fikun
rows.why: لغة is feminine; Amal's 'بس لغة as well' prompted, he said 'Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema'. The verb stayed fikun (feminine would be tkoon) and was not fixed.
rows.english: The language will be important to them.

rows.medi_said: Um, il modara. No, modara is present... moraja.
rows.why: Asked for the word for 'future' he guessed مضارع and مراجعة (wrong words); Amal began مـ-مس... and gave مستقبل (sheet: Musta2bal = future).

rows.medi_said: How do I say-- Do I know how to say adults? I don't know how to say adults.
rows.amal_said: Just we say the big ones يعني the big. / الكبار.
rows.why: He asked how to say adults; Amal gave the big ones, الكبار.

rows.medi_said: libisna costume bas kul il zgar.
rows.why: Subject is the adults (they) but he said 'we wore' (libisna); Amal said لبسوا and ليش?, he accepted: 'Okay. It would be لبسوا?'
rows.english: Only the adults wore costumes, but all the kids did.

rows.medi_said: Okay. Uh, libsa Halloween. Libsa, right?
rows.why: A feminine first word in idafa grows -t (libset Halloween); Amal recast لبست and he said Libsit.

rows.medi_said: حلو، حلوين كتير، حلوات كتير. -> كان حلووات كتير. كانوا حلوات كتير.
rows.why: He gave the adjective with no 'were'; Amal's 'Where؟' reads as a prompt for 'were' and he added كان then كانوا. The engine may have written 'Were' as 'Where'.

rows.medi_said: كان حلووات كتير. كانوا حلوات كتير. ... كل، كل ولاد.
rows.amal_said: لأ، عاد صغار بس حلوين قول حلوات
rows.why: After 'Are they all girls?' Amal told him which adjective plural to use; he answered 'حلوين' and she said mm-hmm. Her line is garbled, so the direction of the fix is uncertain.

rows.medi_said: كل حدا، جابوا واحد أكلة.
rows.amal_said: إيه wait. ... now I'm describing one. So jab أو jabu... Cos I'm saying person.
rows.why: كل حدا (every person) is singular so the verb is جاب; Amal explained 'now I'm describing one', he said 'Oh, you're right. جاب.'

rows.medi_said: كل حدا جاب واحد أكل، أكلة. No، واحدة أكلة.
rows.amal_said: آ، واحدة is an adjective. So what do where do I put it؟
rows.why: The adjective goes after the noun; Amal asked where to put it and he fixed to أكلة واحدة (her صح).

rows.medi_said: كل عيلتها، طلبوني.
rows.why: 'Ask someone to do' is طلب من; طلبوني means they requested me. Amal said 'No', he tried عليّ، لي, then مني.
rows.english: Her whole family asked me (to bring kebab).

rows.medi_said: طلبوا مني، آآ، إنه جبت kebab.
rows.why: After 'asked me' the second verb is a bare present (أجيب), not past; Amal said 'to bring', he asked 'just جيب؟', she gave أجيب kebab.
rows.english: They asked me to bring kebab.

rows.medi_said: شو الكلمة spinach؟
rows.why: He asked for the word; Amal gave سبانخ (sheet: spinach | sabane5 | سبانخ).

rows.medi_said: بيضة. / مثل بيضة like eggs and cheese, right؟
rows.amal_said: لا، لا. It's a type of cheese. جبنة بيضا. / لا، يعني white cheese.
rows.why: He took her جبنة بيضا (white cheese) for egg and repeated بيضة twice; Amal said no, white cheese. Listening miss.

rows.medi_said: يوم الثلاث،
rows.why: Asked what day it is he named the wrong day; Amal said No and he gave يوم الاثنين (sheet: monday).

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم. / أنا بأسب لهم / عليه
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Saħħ
rows.why: 'Upset for someone' takes 3ala (sheet: Ana batDaaya2 3ala); he tried منهم and لهم, she said Mm-mm each time, then Saħħ for alayhom.

rows.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. / Mm-hmm. I got.
rows.why: The English prompt was past ('I got upset'); he used a present b- verb, Amal said 'I got', he answered 'Oh, you're right' and used daia et.

rows.medi_said: Alayhom ala...
rows.why: He tried to add a preposition before 'the end of the movie'; Amal said no, you don't need anything.
rows.english: at the end of the movie

rows.medi_said: Akher. No, tahet. / Under. / Uh, tahet.
rows.amal_said: La saħħ. Shu yammi taħet. It's not taħet.
rows.why: He said akher first, then switched to tahet (under); Amal rejected tahet. He returned to akher il film (Saħħ, mumtaz).

rows.medi_said: أنا جاوبت على أغلب من-- أغلب الـ، أغلب السؤال
rows.why: aghlab takes a definite noun, not من; Amal answered Mm. Mm. Il., he got to أسئلة. Medi later says 'I said أغلب من and you corrected me'.
rows.english: I answered most of the questions.

rows.medi_said: So أول الـ اجتماع، أسوأ من-- Oh, كان أسوأ
rows.why: Missing kaan for 'was worse'; he added كان in the same line and Amal said 'Was.' just after. Possibly his own self-fix.
rows.english: The beginning of the meeting was worse.

rows.medi_said: من الـ آخر.
rows.amal_said: The end of it. / Just it. / صح، آخره.
rows.why: 'The end of it' needs the pronoun on the word and no el-; Amal hinted 'Just it', he guessed آخر هي هو؟ then آخره, she said صح.

rows.medi_said: منيح بس ما حبيت الـ آخرو.
rows.amal_said: No ال. Why? / Why no ال؟
rows.why: A word with a possessive ending never takes el-; Amal said 'No ال. Why?' and he said 'Oh, 'cause it's conjugated.'
rows.english: I didn't like the end of it.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول أكل-- الـ أول أكلين؟ No.
rows.why: He built a non-word أكلين; Amal asked what it means; he dropped it and started over with أول الفيلم.
rows.english: (trying to build a sentence with أول)

rows.medi_said: No، إشي غير من هم.
rows.why: غير goes before the noun; Amal said 'غير إشي، ليش؟' and he stated the rule 'غير always comes before the noun'.

rows.medi_said: Isn't it مواسف؟ No? ... Would it be مواسف here or would it be ياسر؟
rows.amal_said: ماسب is angry، بس angering. / بيعصب
rows.why: He asked for the adjective angering; Amal answered بيعصب (sheet: m3asseb angry). The engine garbled his word.

rows.medi_said: كان angering.
rows.amal_said: بيعصب بس كان أو كانوا cuz أخبار is multiple news.
rows.why: أخبار is plural so the verb should be plural (كانوا); Amal explained 'أخبار is multiple news'.

rows.medi_said: أوّل الصباح، أو بيعصبوا.
rows.why: He left out kaan for 'were angering'; Amal said 'they were' and he said Oh، أو كانو بيعصبوا.

rows.medi_said: الحرب راح يسير أسوأ
rows.why: حرب is feminine so ra7 tseer; he repeated with راح تصير أسوأ and Amal said صح. May be his own fix; also a س/ص sound.
rows.english: The war is going to get worse.

rows.medi_said: مش بتوجع مع حرب؟ حرب؟ ... I don't know the plural for حرب.
rows.why: Asked for the plural of war he could not give it; Amal said 'We learned it' and he recalled حروب (sheet: war | 7arb).

rows.medi_said: لما أنا أطلع الطبيعة
rows.why: Look at needs the verb أتطلع + على; Amal said 'أطلع at.' and he said أتطلع على الطبيعة.

rows.medi_said: لما أنا أطلع الطبيعة
rows.why: Wrong form of the verb (أطلع go out vs أتطلع look at); he said 'I even knew that before'.

rows.medi_said: No, your صحابك تانيين.
rows.why: After a definite noun (it has a pronoun) the adjective takes el-: صحابك التاني; Amal: 'close', then التاني and the explanation.

rows.medi_said: عائلتي, my other family, it would be التاني.
rows.why: عائلة is feminine, so التانية; Amal recast.

rows.medi_said: هذي أول مرة أول يومي هون.
rows.why: 'This is my first day': يوم is masculine, so هذا; Amal said هذا. He mixed مرة with يوم.
rows.english: This is my first day here.

rows.medi_said: أول يومي ... هذي أول اليومي هون
rows.why: أول + a noun with a pronoun means the beginning of my day, not my first day; Amal said 'No' and gave the hint to treat أول as an adjective.

rows.medi_said: يوم الأول.
rows.why: The noun lost its pronoun; Amal said 'يوم هو' and he said يومي الأول (her صح).
